01 / THE CHALLENGE

The challenge

Early teams need visibility across leads, partners and service readiness. When that information is scattered, founder reviews become a bottleneck.

02 / THE APPROACH

The approach

Designed three connected operating systems: a unified CRM, KPI dashboards for onboarding and service readiness, and SOPs for partner onboarding, customer coordination and launch execution. Managed requirements, technical dependencies, adoption blockers and follow-ups across 11 healthcare and eldercare partners.

03 / WHAT CHANGED

What changed

Reported daily founder review time fell from approximately four hours to 50 minutes, an approximately 80% reduction. Eleven partners completed onboarding and operational readiness. Coordinated the first paid caregiver cohort’s launch and built a 200+ member caregiver community.

IN THE DETAILS

Making readiness visible

The CRM brought customer and partner status into a shared view. Dashboards tracked onboarding progress, engagement and service readiness. SOPs clarified handoffs so the founder could spend less time gathering updates and more time prioritising the business.

IN THE DETAILS

A community that informed the service

Monthly webinars, peer discussions and structured feedback created a research and acquisition channel. The 200+ member caregiver community generated 35 customer discovery conversations; membership and conversations are separate measures.

IN THE DETAILS

From preparation to paid service

Coordinated lead qualification, family onboarding, service-delivery dependencies and readiness audits for the first paid cohort. Partner onboarding is separate from signed commercial conversion; cohort revenue, retention and enrolment figures are not claimed here.

THE TAKEAWAY

A good operating system gives people a shared view of what matters and makes the next action obvious.
